correctness.rationale: The closure lemma follows by checking each part of the compatibility definition; the largest/minimal element is a singleton witness when the zero fiber has no more than one nonzero offset, forcing |S|>=w+3 for w>=2. In the explicit construction parity separates translated zero and one fibers and a bidirected path forces all k centers. The indicator of T+T is a direct two-step non-idempotence witness. Small-memory boundary m=2,3,4 is explicitly attained. A standard-library checker independently passes 4258 finite test instances, but universality rests on the supplied proof.

value.rationale: The recent criterion requires searching arbitrary compatible active-center subsets; its two-center example disproves singleton sufficiency. The new theorem exactly answers the motivated worst-case minimum witness-size question for every neighborhood cardinal m>=2. Optimal k+3 constructions prove unbounded indispensable sets even for binary one-dimensional automata; the bound is sharp and uses genuine neighborhood size rather than an arbitrary slice. No unsupported computational complexity lower bound is claimed.
